newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits declined last week, the Labour Department said Friday.
Claims for first-time jobless benefits fell to 335,000 in the week ended Dec. 21 from 350,000 in the week ended Dec. 14. The department originally reported claims of 351,000 in the Dec. 14 period.
The decline in claims last week was sharper than expected. Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 346,000.

The four-week moving average, considered a more accurate gauge of employment trends because it smooths out weekly volatility, edged down slightly last week. It stood at 341,250, down from 342,250 in the previous week.
The department said 18 states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Dec. 14, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Michigan with 6,255 fewer, Pennsylvania with 5,070, Missouri with 3,581, Wisconsin with 3,196 and Illinois with 2,752.
Michigan reported fewer layoffs in the automobile industry, while Pennsylvania had fewer layoffs in food, transportation, construction and services.
In Missouri, Wisconsin and Illinois there were fewer layoffs in construction. Wisconsin and Illinois also had layoffs in services and manufacturing.
Labour said four states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Dec 14 week.
They were Texas with an increase of 6,005, Virginia with 1,924, Ohio with 1,397 and New Jersey with 1,387.
Texas reported layoffs in primary metals, leather goods. Virginia had layoffs in textiles, apparel and furniture.
Ohio said there were layoffs in various industries throughout the state, and New Jersey cited layoffs in construction, trade and services.
